about.title: Laguna Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Laguna Hills carry unique legal hurdles that most personal injury claims don't face. California's MICRA law imposes a short discovery-based deadline, a mandatory 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider, and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the case before it can move forward. Residents here rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and larger Orange County hospital systems, and errors can happen at any point along that chain of care. We review what happened, request the necessary records, and explain whether MICRA's requirements can be met in your situation. A bad outcome alone doesn't mean malpractice occurred, so early legal guidance matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Laguna Hills Families Choose Us

items.title: We Understand MICRA's Tight Timeline
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, capped at three years from the injury itself, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so we move quickly to evaluate your case.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into the Process
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim. We work with medical experts who can assess whether the standard of care was actually breached.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, Ever
items.desc: We handle malpractice cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You can explore your options without financial risk while MICRA's non-economic damages cap and other rules are explained clearly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Laguna Hills?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA law, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice to the healthcare provider before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines are strict, it's worth speaking with us as soon as possible.

items.question: Is a poor medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves uncertainty, and a bad result doesn't by itself prove negligence. California requires a qualified medical expert to evaluate whether the provider's care fell below the accepted standard, which is why an early review matters.

items.question: Does it matter which Laguna Hills facility treated me?
items.answer: It can. Whether care happened at a local urgent care clinic, a physician's office along Moulton Parkway or Alicia Parkway, or a larger Orange County hospital, the records and staff involved will shape how the claim is investigated. We can help identify which providers and records are relevant to your situation.

items.question: What do you charge for a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We provide free case reviews, and we work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can reach out to discuss your medical malpractice concern at no cost.
